coreClinicalTrainingExperiences.emergencyDepartmentHIVConsultation: Fellows provide 24/7 ER consultations at LAC+USC for patients with new, acute, or chronic HIV, offering bedside education to emergency staff.

hivSubspecialtyCare.description: Training occurs mainly at 5p21, with rotations at MCA Clinic, CHLA, and UC San Diego Owen’s Clinic. Focus areas include:

coreClinicalTrainingExperiences.inpatientCare: Fellows train in management of hospitalized HIV-positive patients at LAC+USC. They rotate on the USC ID Consult Service for at least one month, functioning as co-fellows with ID fellows and assisting in care of HIV and non-HIV patients with infectious disease pathology.

teachingTrainingOpportunities: Develop advanced teaching skills by leading sessions for patients, students, and healthcare professionals. Each fellow creates at least one original HIV-related interactive presentation.

Clinical Training Program (CTP): A hands-on 1–2 week preceptorship for providers. Fellows lead HIV orientation workshops, small group OI cases, standardized patient exercises, and serve as preceptors in clinic.
Emergency Department Testing & Linkage: Fellows teach patients, ER staff, and trainees about HIV basics, testing algorithms, OI diagnosis, ART initiation, and linkage-to-care strategies.
Los Angeles County Jail: Fellows support training for new staff and providers, offering HIV/HCV updates and orientations.
Deliver lectures on HIV topics at local teaching sites, including White Memorial Medical Center, USC School of Dentistry, USC PA Program, and USC AETC projects.
